references.text: Moses collects the blood in basins and sprinkles half of it on the altar, as preparation for making a covenant with the people.
The blood was used as a sign of covenant and protection during the Passover in Egypt, a precursor to the covenant blood.
Sprinkling blood on the altar is part of the sacrificial rituals that confirm the covenant between God and Israel.
The blood is given for atonement on the altar, explaining the central role of blood in the covenant relationship.
The expression 'to cut a covenant' (כָּרַת בְּרִית) is used here regarding God's covenant with Abraham.
The people's pledge to keep the covenant, confirmed by sprinkling with blood in chapter 24.
The prophet refers to the covenant blood as the basis for freeing captives.
The book of Hebrews quotes directly from Exodus 24:8 and explains how the first covenant was inaugurated with blood.
Jesus uses the words 'this is my blood, the blood of the new covenant' at the Last Supper, alluding to Exodus 24:8.
Jesus refers to the covenant blood at the institution of the Lord's Supper.
Luke's account of the Last Supper with reference to the new covenant in Jesus' blood.
Paul quotes Jesus' words about the new covenant in his blood.
Refers to the blood of the covenant that sanctifies believers, in contrast to the blood of the old covenant.
Jesus' blood speaks better than Abel's blood, pointing to the superiority of the new covenant.
Peter mentions sprinkling with the blood of Jesus Christ as part of salvation.
The Letter to the Hebrews fulfills and interprets Exodus' covenant ritual by identifying Jesus' blood as the foundation of the final covenant.
Both verses confirm that the covenant is established specifically 'on the basis of' the stated words, which underscores the central role of the law in the covenant relationship.
The people's consent in chapter 19 is the necessary prerequisite for the covenant-making with blood in chapter 24.
